meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-10 | Time: 16:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Redwood: Maya Chen, Diego Ramos | Customer: Aisha, Ben, Priya, Liam
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we've got about 45 minutes. i'm maya from Redwood, this is diego our SE. can you do quick intros?
00:10 Aisha Malik: sure, i'm aisha, eng manager at triton retail, ben's on backend, priya security, liam is our cto. we're evaluating inference options for our customer chat and product tagging pipelines.
00:22 Diego Ramos: awesome, today we'll focus on the SDK quickstarts - python and typescript - auth patterns and a brief console/optimize walkthrough, then next steps for a POC.
00:35 Ben Koh: high level question, are the SDKs just thin wrappers over the REST API? we prefer ts server usage.
00:42 Maya Chen: good q, yes they're lightweight clients around the REST endpoints; the TS SDK works server-side (node) and we have a python lib for sync/async. we also have code examples for streaming and function/tool calling.
00:58 Priya Nair: for security: we need SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. is that supported out of the box?
01:05 Maya Chen: yes, we support SAML SSO for console access, RBAC for teams, audit logs exported to your SIEM, and KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments. for hosted API keys we store keys encrypted; for private/dedicated customers you can bring your own KMS.
01:25 Liam O'Connor: and data residency - can we keep logs in eu region?
01:29 Diego Ramos: absolutely, we can route requests to EU regions and we offer private deployments for stricter controls. for hosted we have region pinning and retention controls.
01:44 Diego Ramos: ok quick demo - python quickstart. the usual flow is pip install redwood, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, then from redwood import Client, client = Client()... (audio) example: response = client.generate(prompt=...)
02:05 Ben Koh: how are retries/timeout handled in the SDK? we have service-to-service timeouts.
02:10 Diego Ramos: the SDK exposes a timeout param and automatic exponential backoff for 5xx/429 by default; you can customize middleware. we also surface token-level metrics in the console for per-route latency.
02:25 Aisha Malik: for typescript, is streaming supported over SSE/websocket?
02:30 Diego Ramos: yes, the TS SDK supports streaming via EventSource and web socket examples. we also show nginx and cloud-load-balancer configs in the repo.
02:47 Maya Chen: auth patterns: simple API key for evals and quickstarts; for POC we recommend service accounts with scoped keys. for enterprise you can do SAML + SCIM provisioning for user access.
03:02 Priya Nair: if we do dedicated, where do keys live? can they be rotated automatically?
03:07 Diego Ramos: keys can be rotated; for private deployments keys are in your KMS and Redwood integrates using customer-managed encryption. rotation is supported via the console or API.
03:22 Ben Koh: what's the recommended env setup for local dev vs prod? any docker examples?
03:26 Diego Ramos: yes, repo has docker-compose and k8s job examples. local dev: use a sandbox API key with short TTL and enable request logging. prod: use service account, store keys in vault or cloud secret manager, enable prefix caching and per-route batching in config.
03:45 Aisha Malik: you mentioned Optimize - can it recommend batching/quantization automatically?
03:50 Maya Chen: Optimize analyzes your workload and suggests batching sizes, cache rules (prefix caching), and quantization profiles per model to hit latency/cost targets. it's part of the Console recommendations tab.
04:05 Liam O'Connor: for POC benchmarking - how do we measure cost/latency? do you provide a harness?
04:11 Diego Ramos: we provide a benchmark harness and can run in your account or ours. typical POC compares hosted vs dedicated under your QPS and sequence length distribution. we output token-level cost, p95 latency, and throughput.
04:28 Priya Nair: auditability - are request/response logs redacted by default? what about PII?
04:33 Maya Chen: by default we redact sensitive fields and you can configure additional redaction rules. for private deployments you control retention and full logs can stay in your VPC.
04:48 Ben Koh: any gotchas on TypeScript typings for streaming events?
04:51 Diego Ramos: we ship types for the SDK; streaming callbacks use a union type that you'll see in the repo - occasional mismatch in auto-gen docs, but the typings are pretty stable.
05:05 Aisha Malik: ok this is helpful. can you walk through the console briefly?
05:09 Maya Chen: sure, i'm sharing screen (audio note: screen share walkthrough). console has routes (mapping endpoints to models), dashboards (latency/cost by route), rollouts (canary, percentage-based), and recommendations from Optimize. you can pin model versions per route.
05:38 Liam O'Connor: on rollouts, is there automatic fallback if a canary fails?
05:42 Diego Ramos: yes you can set health thresholds and automatic rollback, or fallback to a cheaper model variant.
05:52 Priya Nair: last question - sample code for SAML automation?
05:56 Maya Chen: we have a SAML guide plus SCIM provisioning scripts in the security docs - i'll share the links.
06:06 Maya Chen: recap / next steps: we'll send the python/typescript quickstart repos, SOC2 and SSO docs to Priya, schedule the benchmark for week of 12/15, and provide pricing for dedicated 3-gpu option.
06:20 Aisha Malik: thanks, please cc liam and priya on the security docs.
06:24 Maya Chen: absolutely. any final Qs?
06:27 Ben Koh: none from me.
06:28 Liam O'Connor: all good.
06:30 Maya Chen: great, we'll follow up with the artifacts. thanks everyone.
06:34 [call ends]
